steps.text: Combine whipping cream, grated Parmesan cheese, and butter in a medium saucepan. Cook and stir over medium-low heat until smooth. Remove from heat; sauce will thicken as it sits.

review.reviewBody:
To all those who have criticized this recipe, here are a few notes:

1. Use fresh parmesan, grated (many reviewers say they HAVE, but...)

2. Add it SLOWLY -- don't dump the whole amount of cheese in at one time. Add it a half cup at a time, and keep stirring, and wait 3 or so minutes, and....

3. Put the heat on medium, not medium low, and....

4. Stir constantly, and...

5. Recognize it can be a BASE. For those of you who like more flavor, add garlic or onions or oregano or hot sauce or whatever you want.

It's fine as it is, when made properly. If you want more flavors, or want it thicker, or want it thinner, correct as you go.

My husband is very particular about his Alfredo sauce. As in, he still talks about the sauce from the restaurant we frequented when we lived in a town over 14 years ago. I made this and he said it was as good as that recipe. Also, I am not a big fan of just any Alfredo. This sauce is extremely easy, and so tasty! 

The only changes I made were to add fresh ground pepper and a little garlic powder for seasoning. (We usually go heavy on garlic - I didn't need to here. This really is fabulous!)

Also, I started out stirring with a wooden spoon. The cheese was not combining smoothly, so I did switch to stirring with a whisk, and it made all the difference in texture. I also agree this has to be made with fresh grated Parmesan. I made it once on the fly when I only had the powdered. The flavor was good, but the sauce came out somewhat gritty (like the texture of the powdered Parmesan cheese) and thinner, so I added extra cheese. I was using as a mix rather than as a stand-alone, so it worked out ok, but I would not recommend if you can use the better quality cheese.

I added fresh minced garlic to the butter as the butter was melting. Wonderful flavor but my sauce was on the thin side. Not sure what I did wrong. FWIW I used unsalted butter, exactly 1pint of heavy whipping cream & a cup and a half of fresh grated Parmesan that I grated from a brick of Parmesan. Definitely going to make again. FWIW2 I served this sauce with Fettuccine noodles and I grilled over charcoal, Greenwise skin on chicken thighs which I deboned just before grilling. Again, loved the flavor of the sauce but I need to figure out why my sauce was a tad on the thin side

cook the cream slowly and i jazzed it up a bit added a few seasonings. 2 teaspoons of garlic powder 2 teaspoon chives 1 teaspoon tarragon 1/2 teaspoon of marjoram 1 teaspoon of parsley 1/4 teaspoon of salt 1/8 teaspoon of pepper and 1/2 teaspoon of basil grind and blend all spices in mortar and add to cream mixture at the beginning to give time for flavor release these are approximate measurements on spices because i usually just add until it looks and smells to my liking came out great.

This is the perfect base sauce! Since there are few things my kids will eat, and this is one of their favorites, we have this once a week for pasta night. I use unsalted real butter, Frigo shaved Parmesan cheese, and just Great Value brand whipping cream. I dump all three ingredients in the pan at once and then set my burner to the "melt" setting. Just put it on the lowest setting if yours doesn't have a "melt" function. I keep it this low until the butter is completely melted, stirring occasionally. Once the butter is melted, crank it up to medium and let the cheese start melting...it WILL melt and meld, promise! Once the cheese is melted and it's all stringy, I crank up the heat another couple of notches and let it come to a rolling boil, stirring constantly. Let it boil one minute...that's how you get it smooth. Now let's talk flavor. I like very flavorful alfredo sauce. I add salt to taste, several fresh basil leaves, and garlic powder to taste. I add these extras at the beginning. Hope that helps for those of you saying this was bland or that their were timing issues with melting the cheese!

Not very good in my humble opinion.

Leave out all of the butter. 

Put 2 cloves of minced garlic in a hot skillet and then add the heavy whipping creme. Bring it to a slow boil and add your pre cooked fettuccine noddles. Then add fresh grated Parmesan cheese to get the thickness you prefer. Done! 

You can add some pesto if you want.

This was a last minute decision to make Alfredo sauce with some tri color fresh tortellini tonight. I made half the recipe which was perfect for the amount of pasta.
I also added 1 tsp sea salt, 2 turns of black pepper from my grinder, 1 crushed dry garlic slice and 1/4 cup diced mozzarella.
I added the cream to partially melted butter and gradually added the cheese while stirring. 
The sauce was GREAT on the tortellini with 1/4 cup petite peas and 2 Tbsp crumbled bacon.
I will definitely make this again.

Delish! Heated the cream slowly then added small pieces of butter at a time. Then added the Parmesan cheese in batches & stirred constantly. I added some garlic powder then poured the sauce over penne (daughter’s favorite) & added broccoli that was steamed in chicken broth and some sliced boneless, skinless chicken that I grilled with salt, pepper, garlic powder & extra virgin olive oil. Can’t wait for my daughter to get home from work & have some!

I loved this recipe. It is not bad at all. I encourage you to follow the recommendations from CHEFSINGLEDAD. If you do, you should not be disappointed. The key is to be PATIENT to let the cheese melt properly at MEDIUM heat while stirring it and do not toss the cheese all at once. I also use a whisker to make sauces and for this particular one I use a hint of nutmeg. I did not have grated parmesan. I had shredded and it came out perfectly fine following his suggestions. Put salt and pepper to your taste...
Read the reviews. Used fresh grated parmesan cheese. Good decision as the sauce was very creamy. Let the sauce rest to thicken. Perfect. A keeper recipe.

To anyone who rated this anything else but 5 stars; I've cooked and managed many popular restaurants including The Olive Garden, TGI Fridays and Applebees to name a few. This is the exact way we made our Alfredo sauce, the trick is, as others have mentioned, is to keep the heat at medium as a friend minimum. Next is to add the FRESH Parmesan cheese last and no more than a 1/2 cup at a time! When you get ready to add the Parmesan cheese it is crucial that the sauce be hot, not a full boil hot, but a slow, consistent boil. Otherwise the cheese won't melt and incorporate into the sauce. Don't be afraid to play with the recipe to make it more to your liking, for instance, adding garlic from fresh crushed to garlic powder or salt. Fresh basil, oregano or parsley are other common add ons, but make sure you have the basic recipe down before you play with it. Don't be frustrated or quit if it doesn't come out right the first time you make it, even professional chefs have to remake it occasionally, yes it's a simple recipe with only simple ingredients but it requires timing and technique.
Such an easy receipt, my grandson made it twice, while he was visiting during summer vacation. He loved it so much I had to print it out so he could make it at home!
I added another 1/2 cheese, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Simple and delicious
Great recipe. I don’t buy Alfredo sauce anymore

I had to use my own seasoning, salt, pepper and Italian seasoning. And I don't pour the cheese in all at once. I pour a little bit out of a thyme stirring so it gives it time to melt. It comes out pretty thick. So I would add a little bit of starch water from the pasta.

I found this recipe nearly 16 years ago. It's the recipe that I go to first when making an Alfredo sauce. This sauce is extremely versatile. I have made it exactly as written with positive results every time. I do like to spruce it up a bit when I'm feeling a bit adventurous. Adding freshly shredded/grated Parmesan gives it a beautiful nutty flavor; it adds creaminess to the sauce. The recipe, as it's written, is a base recipe. It's a blank slate for adding flavor. I prefer to add some minced garlic in the sauce and parsley on top of the sauce.
My family absolutely love this Alfredo. I've made it several times.
Honestly this is the best, easiest, quickest Alfredo I’ve ever made! I used a good quality Parmesan and added some garlic & back pepper. Tasted restaurant-quality!
